sections.name: SearchAPIProvider
sections.title: The SearchAPI provider
sections.what: Reports itself available when the key is set. When searched, it sends a Google query and maps the results to the shared shape. Returns nothing on error or timeout.
sections.why: Likely reason: a simple, single-key provider where errors are logged and skipped so other providers still answer.
sections.watch_out: Errors return an empty list, so an exhausted quota looks like a search with no results.

summary: Searches Google through the SearchAPI.io service using one API key and returns up to 10 web results.
purpose: One paid web search source that feeds Google-style results into the combined search.
why: Reason for the specific limits is not stated in the code; the timeout is a named constant.
how: Checks that a key is set, then sends a search request with the query, the Google engine, and a result count capped at 10, aborting after 15 seconds. Each organic result becomes a standard result with its link, title, snippet cut to 500 characters, and date. Any failure logs a short warning and returns nothing.
inputs: The query text, the maximum result count, and the SEARCHAPI_KEY setting.
outputs: Standard search results, labelled with source searchapi and authority score 0. The router sets the real score later.
risks: The key is part of the request address, so logging full addresses would expose it. There is no backup key, so a quota error returns nothing. Results are not trimmed to the requested count if the service returns more.
debug: Check the searchapi log lines for HTTP errors or timeouts. Confirm the key is set, and check the active provider list logged at startup.
